mainTopic: Competing קידושין by a שליח and the principal, and the dispute between רב and שמואל on whether a girl's present בגרות reaches back in time.
overview: The amud finishes the משנה about a father, or a woman, who sent a שליח to arrange קידושין and then made קידושין personally. Whichever קידושין came first counts. If nobody knows which came first, both men give a גט. The גמרא explains why both cases are needed: a father knows lineage, and a woman is careful about whom she marries. Next, רב and שמואל argue about a father who betrothed his daughter on the road while she betrothed herself in the city, when she is now a בוגרת. The גמרא sets the case on the exact day her six months of נערות ended. רב says her present status reaches back to the morning, while שמואל says she may have become a בוגרת only now. The גמרא challenges שמואל from a lacking מקוה and from a barrel of wine found turned to vinegar. Each time it answers that those cases have two weaknesses against the old status, while hers has only one. Finally, the גמרא suggests that the dispute matches an argument between תנאים, and that source continues on the next amud.

steps.title: When it is unknown whose betrothal came first, both give a divorce
steps.stepSummary: This ends the משנה's first case, the father and his שליח. If it is unknown which קידושין came first, both men give a גט. Or one gives a גט and the other marries her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both give a divorce document. And if they want, one gives a divorce document and the other marries her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its rule about a father who sent a שליח to betroth his daughter and then betrothed her himself. If we don't know which happened first, she needs a גט from both men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One of the two קידושין is surely valid, but we don't know which one. So she cannot marry anyone else until both men release her with a גט. The two men may also agree that one gives a גט and the other keeps her as his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: A divorce document that ends a marriage or a betrothal
Brings her in as his wife, marries her
Both of them

phrases.english: both give a divorce document.
And if they wish,
one gives a divorce document, and the other marries her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה's first case, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When it is unknown whether the father's or the שליח's קידושין came first, both men give a גט. Or one gives a גט and the other marries her.

steps.title: The same rule for a woman who appointed an agent and then betrothed herself
steps.stepSummary: A woman who sent a שליח to accept קידושין for her and then accepted קידושין herself follows the same rule. The earlier קידושין is valid. If nobody knows which came first, both men give a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same applies to a woman who let her agent betroth her and then went and betrothed herself. If hers came first, her betrothal is valid. If the agent's came first, his is valid. If they don't know, both give her a divorce document, or if they want, one gives a divorce document and the other marries her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same rule to a woman who appointed a שליח and then accepted קידושין on her own. Whichever קידושין happened first is the one that counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is the same as the father's case. Only the person who appointed the שליח is different. The rule is that time decides: the first קידושין takes effect, and the second one has nothing to take hold of. When the order is unknown, she needs a גט from both men.

keyTerms.meaning: Permission, authorization
Her agent, her שליח
Came first
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

phrases.english: And similarly, a woman
who gave permission to her agent to betroth her,
and she went and betrothed herself,
if her own came first,
her betrothal is a valid betrothal,
and if her agent's came first,
his betrothal is a valid betrothal.
phrases.notes: "His betrothal" means the קידושין the שליח accepted for her from the man he chose.

phrases.english: And if they do not know which came first,
both give her a divorce document,
and if they wish,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד נוֹתֵן לָהּ גֵּט וְאֶחָד כּוֹנֵס.
phrases.english: one gives her a divorce document and the other marries her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁנָּתְנָה רְשׁוּת לִשְׁלוּחָהּ לְקַדְּשָׁהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second case that follows the same rule as the father's case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman's own קידושין and her שליח's קידושין follow the order in time. If the order is unknown, she needs a גט from both men.
steps.whatToRemember: Whoever acts first, the person or the שליח, makes the קידושין that counts. If nobody knows who was first, both men must give a גט.

steps.title: Why the woman's case is needed: a man knows lineage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that both cases are needed. From the father's case alone, we might have said that only a man's own קידושין overrides his שליח, because he is an expert in lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary to teach both. If the משנה had taught us only about the father, I would say his betrothal counts because a man knows family lineage well. But a woman, who doesn't know lineage well, I would say her betrothal does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a צריכותא, explaining why the משנה had to teach two cases that look the same. This step explains why the father's case alone would not be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father knows family lineage (יוחסין). So when he goes ahead on his own, we assume he found a better match and wants to cancel the שליח. A woman might not trust her own judgment about lineage. So we might think she still wants her שליח to find someone better, and her own קידושין would not count. The משנה teaches that her קידושין is valid too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary, both cases are needed
It taught us
He knows well, he is an expert
Family lineage and pedigree
I would say, I might have thought

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that a woman's קידושין really is invalid. It is only describing a mistake we could have made if the משנה had taught the father's case alone.

phrases.english: Gemara: And it is necessary to teach both cases,
for if it had taught us only about him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the father from the first case of the משנה.

phrases.english: I would say that is because a man
is an expert in lineage,
but a woman,
who is not an expert in lineage,
I might say her betrothal should not be a valid betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the משנה needed to repeat the rule for a woman after teaching it for a father.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the father's case alone we could not learn the woman's case, because the father's knowledge of lineage gives a reason that does not apply to her.

steps.title: Why the father's case is needed: a woman is careful about her match
steps.stepSummary: From the woman's case alone, we might have said that only she overrides her שליח, because she is very careful about whom she marries. A father may not care as much. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught us only about her, I would say it is because a woman checks carefully before she marries. But about him, I would say he doesn't care. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא by showing that the woman's case alone would not teach us the father's case. It then concludes that the משנה needed both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman is marrying for herself, so she checks carefully. If she picked a husband herself, she clearly no longer wants her שליח to act. A father might not care as much about whom his daughter marries. So we might think his שליח's קידושין still counts even after the father acted. Each case has its own reason, so neither can be learned from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: She is careful, she checks closely
She gets married
He does not care

steps.whatToRemember: Both cases are needed. A father's act counts because he knows lineage. A woman's act counts because she is careful about her own match. Either way, the first קידושין is the valid one.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only about her,
I would say that is because a woman checks carefully and then marries,
but as for him,
phrases.notes: "Him" means the father who appointed a שליח for his daughter.

phrases.english: I might say he does not care,
therefore it is necessary to teach both.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא by giving the reverse reason and concluding that both cases are needed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה needs both the father's case and the woman's case, because each has a separate reason that would not carry over to the other.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about a father's and daughter's competing betrothals
steps.stepSummary: A father betrothed his daughter on the road, and she betrothed herself in the city. She is now a בוגרת. רב says she counts as a בוגרת. שמואל says we worry that both קידושין may be valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: her father betrothed her on the road, and she betrothed herself in the city, and now she is a grown woman. רב said: She is a grown woman in front of us. And שמואל said: We are concerned about the betrothal of both of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new dispute between רב and שמואל. The case is a father's קידושין competing with the daughter's own קידושין, when she is now a בוגרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father can marry off his daughter only until she becomes a בוגרת. After that, only she can accept קידושין. רב judges her by what we see now: she is a בוגרת, so the father's קידושין did not take effect. שמואל is unsure, so he treats both קידושין as possibly valid.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated: introduces a dispute between אמוראים
A grown woman, past the six months of נערות. Her father can no longer betroth her.
In front of us: judging by her status as we see it now
We are concerned: we treat it as a real doubt

phrases.english: It was stated: Her father betrothed her on the road,
and she betrothed herself in the city,
and now she is a grown woman.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: הֲרֵי הִיא בּוֹגֶרֶת לְפָנֵינוּ.
phrases.english: רב said: She is a grown woman in front of us.
phrases.notes: He means: go by what we see now. She is a בוגרת, so her father had no power to betroth her.

phrases.english: And שמואל said: We are concerned about the betrothal of both of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. Like the earlier steps, it deals with competing קידושין, but here the question is the girl's age status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: she is treated as a בוגרת now, so the father's קידושין do not take effect. שמואל: both קידושין are a doubt.

steps.title: When did this happen? It can't be during the six months, according to רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the father's קידושין happened. If it was during the six months of נערות, how could רב call her a בוגרת? She only became one now.
steps.simpleTranslation: When? If we say it was within the six months, would רב say in such a case 'she is a grown woman in front of us'? It is only now that she became grown!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to pin down the exact timing of the case. It tests the first option, 'during the six months', against רב's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the six months after she becomes a נערה, she is clearly still a נערה, so her father's קידושין would work. רב could not ignore it just because she is a בוגרת today. So this timing does not fit רב.

keyTerms.meaning: When? Asks for the exact timing of a case
If you say: tests one possible explanation
A young woman during the six months before she becomes a בוגרת. Her father can still betroth her.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Within six' does not mean six months from today. It means during the six months of נערות, before she became a בוגרת.

phrases.english: When?
If we say within the six months,
phrases.notes: The six months of נערות, the stage before she becomes a בוגרת.

phrases.english: in such a case would רב say
'she is a grown woman in front of us'?
It is only now that she became grown!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the timing of the case in step 5, testing the first option against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling, if the case happened during the six months of נערות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: During those months she was certainly a נערה, so the father's קידושין should work. Her later status cannot cancel it.

steps.title: It can't be after the six months, according to שמואל
steps.stepSummary: If the father's קידושין happened after the six months, she was surely a בוגרת already. Then how could שמואל worry about the father's קידושין? שמואל himself says נערות lasts only six months.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was after six months. Would שמואל say in such a case 'we are concerned about the betrothal of both of them'? But שמואל said: Between נערות and בגרות there are only six months!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second option, 'after the six months', and shows it does not fit שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל holds that a girl is a בוגרת exactly six months after becoming a נערה. If the father acted after that point, she was clearly a בוגרת and his קידושין mean nothing. So שמואל would have no reason to worry about them. Neither timing works for both opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: The stage of being a נערה
The stage of being a בוגרת, fully grown
But didn't he say: points out that a person contradicts his own statement

phrases.english: Rather, after the six months,
in such a case would שמואל say:
'We are concerned about the betrothal of both of them'?
But שמואל said:
Between being a young woman and being grown there is nothing
except six months alone!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְאַחַר שִׁשָּׁה, בְּהָא נֵימָא שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first timing failed for רב, the second timing is tested and fails for שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling, if the case happened after the six months
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's own rule says she is a בוגרת exactly after six months. Then the father's קידושין are clearly void, and there is nothing to worry about.

steps.title: The case is on the exact day the six months end
steps.stepSummary: The father betrothed her on the very day the six months finished. רב says that since she is a בוגרת now, she was one this morning too. שמואל says maybe her signs of בגרות only appeared now.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where he betrothed her on the day the six months were completed. רב said: She is a grown woman in front of us. Since she is grown now, she was also grown in the morning. And שמואל said: Maybe it is only now that the signs came.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the case is on the borderline day when the six months end. It then explains each opinion for that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On that day it is unclear whether she was already a בוגרת when her father acted in the morning. רב assumes her present status also applied earlier that day, so the father's קידושין did not work. שמואל says the signs may have appeared only later in the day, so the father's קידושין may be valid. That is why he worries about both.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for: sets the case in a specific situation
Morning
Physical signs of maturity that mark בגרות

steps.whatToRemember: רב: what is true now was true earlier that day. שמואל: the change might have happened only now, so we stay in doubt.

phrases.english: No, it is needed only
where he betrothed her on that day when the six months were completed.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: הֲרֵי הִיא בּוֹגֶרֶת לְפָנֵינוּ,
phrases.english: רב said: She is a grown woman in front of us;
since she is grown now,
she was also grown in the morning.
phrases.notes: The morning is when the father gave his קידושין, earlier that same day.

phrases.english: And שמואל said:
It is only now that she brought signs.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּקַדֵּישׁ בְּהָהוּא יוֹמָא דְּמַשְׁלֵים שִׁשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problems of steps 6 and 7 by placing the case on the borderline day.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setting the case in a narrow situation (לא צריכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case had to be either during or after the six months, and neither fits both opinions.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is on the final day of the six months. The dispute is whether her present status can be applied back to that morning.

steps.title: Challenge to שמואל from a מקוה found lacking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל is different from the case of a מקוה. There, a מקוה found lacking makes everything purified in it in the past impure. That treats the present state as going back in time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to שמואל, how is this different from a מקוה? As we learned in a משנה: A מקוה that was measured and found lacking: all purifications done in it in the past, whether in a private area or a public area, are impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל from a משנה about a מקוה. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a מקוה is measured and found to have too little water, we assume it was already lacking earlier. So everything purified in it in the past becomes impure. That is just like רב's reasoning: the present state goes back in time. So why doesn't שמואל assume she was already a בוגרת in the morning?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? Asks why two similar cases are treated differently
A ritual bath, which must hold a required amount of water
Items made pure (here, by immersion)
Going back in time, retroactively
A public area. Doubts about impurity there are usually treated leniently.

steps.whyThisMatters: The מקוה case is a classic source for applying a present condition back into the past. That idea stands behind רב, and שמואל must explain why he does not use it.

phrases.english: And according to שמואל, how is this different from a ritual bath?
As we learned in a משנה:
A ritual bath that was measured and found lacking:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל טְהָרוֹת שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל גַּבָּיו לְמַפְרֵעַ,
phrases.english: all purifications that were done in it, going back in time,
whether in a private area
or in a public area,
are impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the case is defined, the גמרא challenges שמואל's position from step 8 using a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that her signs may have appeared only now
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the מקוה case, the present lack is assumed to go back into the past. By the same logic, her present בגרות should go back to the morning, which fits רב and not שמואל.

steps.title: The מקוה case is different because the item was impure before
steps.stepSummary: The מקוה case is different. There we can say: keep the impure item in its old impure status and assume it was never properly immersed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because we can say: keep the impure item in its old status, and say it was not immersed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 9. It explains why the מקוה case does not prove anything against שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקוה case, the item already had a status of being impure (a טמא). Keeping that old status supports the conclusion that it is still impure. So the ruling there does not come only from 'what we see now goes back in time.'

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there
Keep it in its old, known status
Ritually impure
Was immersed

phrases.english: It is different there, since one can say:
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of the lacking מקוה from Step 9.

phrases.english: Keep the impure item in its presumptive status
and say it was not immersed.
phrases.notes: He means it was not immersed in a valid מקוה, so it never became pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מקוה challenge against שמואל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מקוה case shows that a present condition always reaches back in time.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the מקוה case, the item's old impure status adds support. That is why the present condition is pushed back there.

steps.title: On the contrary, keep the מקוה in its old full status
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the מקוה also has an old status. It was known to be full, so we should assume it was not lacking.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Keep the מקוה in its old status, and say it was not lacking!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 10. The מקוה has an old status too, and that status points the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side has its own old status. The item used to be impure, but the מקוה used to be full. So the item's old status should not decide the case by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
Was lacking (missing the required amount of water)

phrases.english: On the contrary, keep the מקוה in its presumptive status
phrases.notes: The מקוה was known to have the full required amount of water before.

phrases.english: and say it was not lacking!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the item's old impure status decides the מקוה case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מקוה's old full status cancels out the item's old impure status.

steps.title: The lacking מקוה is right in front of us
steps.stepSummary: The answer: we can see the מקוה is lacking right now, and that weakens its old full status.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a lacking מקוה in front of you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 11. The מקוה's old full status is weak because we can see right now that it is lacking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What we see now works against the מקוה's old status. So the two old statuses are not equal. The item's impure status stands, but the מקוה's full status is undermined.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is in front of you (what we see now)

phrases.english: There is a lacking one before you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: What we see now weakens an old status
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מקוה's old full status is as strong as the item's old impure status.
steps.terutzMaskana: The present lack weakens the מקוה's old status.

steps.title: But here too a בוגרת is in front of us
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: in our case too, we can see she is a בוגרת right now. That should weaken her old status as a נערה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, there is a בוגרת in front of you!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the reasoning of Step 12 and turns it against שמואל's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If seeing something now weakens an old status, then her being a בוגרת now should weaken her old status as a נערה. That would mean she was a בוגרת this morning, which is רב's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too
A girl who has passed נערות and is fully grown

phrases.english: Here too: there is a grown woman before you!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer in Step 12 to challenge שמואל
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's worry that she may have been a נערה when her father betrothed her
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: What we see now should weaken her old status, the same way it does for the מקוה.

steps.title: She may have become a בוגרת only now
steps.stepSummary: The answer: she may have become a בוגרת only now.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only now that she became a בוגרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. Her being a בוגרת now does not prove she was one earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her signs of בגרות may have just appeared. So the present state does not have to reach back to the time of her father's קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: Now
She became a בוגרת

phrases.english: It is only now that she has reached her majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 13
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being a בוגרת now proves she was one earlier.
steps.terutzMaskana: The change may have happened just now.

steps.title: The מקוה could also have become lacking only now
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: then say the same about the מקוה. Maybe it became lacking only now.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too: it is only now that it became lacking!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the answer in Step 14 works just as well for the מקוה. So the two cases still look the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'it only just happened' can protect her status as a נערה, it should also protect the מקוה's full status. Then the items immersed in it should be pure. But the הלכה says they are impure.

keyTerms.meaning: There too

phrases.english: There too: it is only now that it became lacking!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of Step 14 back onto the מקוה case
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference between the מקוה case and the בוגרת case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same 'it just happened' reasoning would make the items in the מקוה pure, which goes against the ruling.

steps.title: Two weaknesses there, only one here
steps.stepSummary: The answer: in the מקוה case there are two weaknesses, but in the בוגרת case there is only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, there are two weaknesses. Here, there is only one weakness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final difference between the cases. This defends שמואל against the מקוה challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקוה case, two things point to impurity: the lacking מקוה we see now, and the item's old impure status. In the daughter's case, only her being a בוגרת now points against her status as a נערה. One weakness is not enough to cancel an old status, so שמואל worries about both קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: Two things weakening the case
Only one thing weakening the case

steps.whatToRemember: An old status falls when two things work against it, like a lacking מקוה plus an item that was impure before. It does not fall when only one thing works against it, like a girl who is a בוגרת now. That is why שמואל still worries she was a נערה.

phrases.english: There, there are two weaknesses,
phrases.notes: The two are the lacking מקוה we see now and the item's old impure status.

phrases.english: here, there is one weakness.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם תַּרְתֵּי לְרֵיעוּתָא, הָכָא חֲדָא לְרֵיעוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 15 and closes the מקוה comparison
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counting the weaknesses in each case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מקוה case and the בוגרת case are the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two weaknesses cancel an old status. One weakness does not.

steps.title: How is שמואל different from the barrel case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how שמואל's view differs from a ברייתא about a barrel of wine found turned to vinegar. Within three days of the last check, it counts as definitely wine. After that, it is a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to שמואל, how is this different from the barrel? As it is taught: a person checked a barrel so that he could keep separating תרומה from it. Later it was found to be vinegar. For all three days after the check, it is definitely wine. From then on, it is a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new comparison and brings a ברייתא about a barrel of wine. It is setting up a new challenge to שמואל, which it will explain next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here too, something we find now (vinegar) raises the question of when the change happened. The full challenge to שמואל comes in step 21: for the רבנן, the vinegar found now reaches back into the past for certain. First, the גמרא clears up a side problem with this ברייתא (steps 18–20).

keyTerms.meaning: Barrel (of wine)
The portion of produce given to a כהן
Vinegar (wine that has gone sour)
Certain
Doubtful

steps.confusionAlert: 'Definitely' means the barrel definitely still counts as wine during those three days. It does not mean it was definitely vinegar.

phrases.english: And according to שמואל, how is it different from a barrel?
As it is taught: one was checking a barrel
in order to keep separating תרומה based on it,
and afterward it was found to be vinegar –
all three days, it is certain,
phrases.notes: The three days after the last check count as definitely wine.

phrases.english: from then on, it is a doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the מקוה comparison, opens a new comparison against שמואל
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that she may still have been a נערה when her father betrothed her
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the רבנן, the vinegar found now makes the wine count as vinegar going back, so wine exempted through it is definitely טבל (step 21). By that logic, her present בגרות should reach back to the morning, against שמואל's doubt.

steps.title: Contradiction between the barrel and the מקוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets the barrel ruling against the מקוה ruling. Why is the מקוה case definite and the barrel case only a doubt?
steps.simpleTranslation: We raised a contradiction between the barrel and the מקוה. Why is one case definite and the other only a doubt?
steps.whatsHappening: Before finishing its question on שמואל, the גמרא first points out a contradiction between two rulings: the barrel of wine and the lacking מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקוה case, everything purified in it since the last check is definitely טמא. In the barrel case, after three days it is only a doubt. Both cases look the same, since in both the problem we see now might reach back into the past, so why do they get different rulings?

keyTerms.meaning: We raised a contradiction (we set two sources against each other)
A barrel (here, the barrel of wine found turned to vinegar)
A ritual bath used for becoming טהור
Definite, certain
A doubt, uncertain

phrases.english: And we raised a contradiction between the barrel and the mikveh:
What is different, that here it is definite,
and what is different, that here it is a doubt?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Before finishing the question on שמואל from step 17, the גמרא first deals with a side problem about the barrel ברייתא itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The barrel ברייתא, compared with the ruling about the מקוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two cases with the same structure, where a problem found now may go back into the past, get different rulings: definite for the מקוה and only a doubt for the barrel.

steps.title: רב חנינא: the barrel ruling follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא מסוריא answers that the barrel ruling follows רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון treats the מקוה case as a doubt too, so there is no contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא מסוריא said: Who taught the barrel case? רבי שמעון, who treats the מקוה case as a doubt too.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנינא מסוריא solves the contradiction. He says the two rulings come from different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The definite ruling on the מקוה belongs to the רבנן. The barrel ruling belongs to רבי שמעון, and he treats both cases as a doubt. Once each ruling has its own author, they no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Who taught this? (asking which תנא holds this view)
He treats it as a doubt

phrases.english: And Rav Chanina from Syria said:
Who taught the barrel case?
It is Rabbi Shimon,
who treats the mikveh case as a doubt too.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תְּנָא חָבִית רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the rulings to different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings come from the same view, so they really contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The barrel ruling follows רבי שמעון, who treats the מקוה as a doubt too. The definite ruling on the מקוה follows the רבנן.

steps.title: ברייתא proving רבי שמעון treats the מקוה as a doubt
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the disagreement. The רבנן say everything purified in the lacking מקוה is definitely טמא. רבי שמעון treats it as a doubt: טהור in a public place, and left undecided in a private place.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: everything purified in it, going back, is טמא, whether in a private or a public place. רבי שמעון says: in a public place it is טהור, and in a private place we leave it undecided.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove what רב חנינא said: רבי שמעון really does treat the מקוה case as a doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן rule טמא everywhere, so for them it is definite. רבי שמעון's ruling only makes sense for a doubt. A doubt about טומאה in רשות הרבים is ruled טהור, and in רשות היחיד it is left hanging. This proves he sees the מקוה case as a doubt, just like the barrel.

keyTerms.meaning: Items that need to stay טהור (pure)
Going back in time, retroactively
A private place
A public place
We leave it hanging: not treated as definitely טהור or definitely טמא

steps.whyThisMatters: The way רבי שמעון splits public from private is the standard way to rule on a doubt about טומאה. So his ruling itself shows he sees the case as a doubt.

phrases.english: As it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל טְהָרוֹת שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל גַּבָּיו לְמַפְרֵעַ,
phrases.english: All pure items that were purified through it, going back,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים –
phrases.english: whether in a private place or in a public place,
are impure.
And Rabbi Shimon says:
in a public place they are pure,
in a private place, we leave them undecided.
phrases.notes: Undecided means we don't eat them, but we also don't burn them as definitely טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא כׇּל טְהָרוֹת שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל גַּבָּיו לְמַפְרֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind רב חנינא's claim in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: רב חנינא's claim that רבי שמעון treats the מקוה case as a doubt
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where the רבנן rule definitely טמא, while רבי שמעון splits public and private places the way one rules on a doubt

steps.title: According to the רבנן, the wine is טבל going back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to its question on שמואל. According to the רבנן, the barrel would make the wine definitely טבל going back, so what we see now decides the past. That doesn't fit שמואל, who treats the woman's case as only a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the רבנן, it is טבל going back!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא finishes the question on שמואל that it started in step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold that what we find now reaches back into the past for certain, as with the מקוה. So for them, wine that was exempted using this barrel would be definitely טבל going back. That clashes with שמואל, who treats the woman's case as only a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority view against רבי שמעון
Produce from which תרומה and מעשרות have not been properly taken

phrases.english: But according to the Rabbis,
it is tevel going back!
phrases.notes: If the wine had already turned to vinegar, it could not exempt other wine. So that other wine was never really fixed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the רבנן's view from the ברייתא in step 20 to finish the challenge to שמואל begun in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the case is only a doubt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For the רבנן, what we see now decides the past for certain, even in the barrel case. That is the opposite of שמואל, who calls it a doubt.

steps.title: The barrel is different: טבל keeps its חזקה
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the barrel case is different. There we can say, keep the טבל in its original status and assume it was never fixed. The certainty comes from that חזקה, not from what we see now.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because we can say: keep the טבל in its original status, and say it was never fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by showing that the barrel case has a special reason to be definite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine starts out as טבל, and that status stays until we know it was fixed. So the רבנן's definite ruling has an extra support: the old חזקה of טבל, which joins with what we see now. In שמואל's case there is no such extra חזקה. The next steps test this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there
Keep it in its original, presumed status
Was fixed (properly tithed)

steps.whatToRemember: This first answer leans on the חזקה of טבל. The next steps challenge it, and the final answer in step 28 combines this חזקה with what we see now.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea: a ruling may be definite because of a separate חזקה, not because of the general rule being argued about.

phrases.english: It is different there,
because one can say:
keep the tevel in its original status,
and say it was not fixed.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר הַעֲמֵד טֶבֶל עַל חֶזְקָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to שמואל from step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Telling the cases apart: a separate חזקה explains the definite ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן's barrel ruling shows that what we find now always decides the past, which goes against שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The barrel is definite only because of the חזקה of טבל. This does not affect שמואל's case.

steps.title: The wine also has a status of its own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the חזקה argument: why not keep the wine in its status as good wine?
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Keep the wine in its original status, and say it had not yet turned to vinegar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 22. If we use a חזקה, why not use the wine's own חזקה, that it was good wine until now?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 said the טבל keeps its original status, so the wine was never fixed. But the wine also has an original status, and it was wine, not vinegar. If we follow that חזקה, the separation would have worked, so the two חזקות seem to cancel each other out.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite argument is just as strong
Keep it in its original, known status
It turned sour, became vinegar

phrases.english: On the contrary,
maintain the wine in its presumptive status,
and say it had not turned to vinegar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the חזקה reasoning of step 22 with an opposing חזקה
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 22 that the barrel case is certain because of the טבל's חזקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wine has its own חזקה of being wine, which points the other way, so the טבל's חזקה should not win automatically.

steps.title: The wine is vinegar right in front of you
steps.stepSummary: The wine's חזקה is weak because we can see it has turned to vinegar.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look, it has turned to vinegar right in front of you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that you cannot lean on the wine's חזקה, because the wine is plainly vinegar now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה of 'it is still wine' is hard to hold onto when the barrel in front of us is vinegar. So the wine's original status is weakened, and the טבל's חזקה remains.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of you; what you can see right now

phrases.english: Look, it is turned to vinegar before you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weakening the opposing חזקה with what we see now
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wine's חזקה is just as strong as the טבל's
steps.terutzMaskana: The wine's חזקה is undermined because it is vinegar now

steps.title: The woman is also a בוגרת right now
steps.stepSummary: If what we see now weakens a status, then the woman, who is a בוגרת now, should lose her status as a נערה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, she is a בוגרת in front of us!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same reasoning against שמואל's case. The woman is clearly a בוגרת now, so that should weaken her old status as a נערה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 let 'what we see now' break the wine's חזקה. By the same reasoning, her being a בוגרת now should break her חזקה of being a נערה. Then her case should be decided too, and should not stay a doubt as שמואל rules.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl who has reached full adulthood, past the stage of נערה
Here too; the same reasoning applies

phrases.english: Here too,
phrases.notes: "Here" means שמואל's case of the woman, which is the case the whole question is about.

phrases.english: she is a grown woman before us!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, הֲרֵי הִיא בּוֹגֶרֶת לְפָנֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the logic of step 24 to שמואל's case
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the woman's case stays a doubt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If her present state as a בוגרת is visible, it should weaken her old חזקה just as the vinegar weakened the wine's.

steps.title: Maybe she only became a בוגרת now
steps.stepSummary: Her present state does not prove much about the past, because she may have grown up only just now.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only now that she became a בוגרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. Seeing her as a בוגרת now does not tell us she was one back then, since she may have just reached that stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a בוגרת today is fully consistent with having been a נערה at the time of the קידושין. So her old status is not really broken, and the doubt remains.

keyTerms.meaning: Now
She became a בוגרת

phrases.english: It is now that she has reached her majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Present state may have only just begun
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her being a בוגרת now proves she was one at the קידושין
steps.terutzMaskana: She may have become a בוגרת only now, so her old status holds

steps.title: Then maybe the wine only soured now
steps.stepSummary: The same answer works for the wine, so the difference between the cases seems to vanish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too: maybe it is only now that it turned to vinegar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns step 26's answer back onto the wine. Maybe the wine also only soured just now, after the separation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'maybe it happened only now' saves the woman's old status, it should save the wine's old status too. Then the barrel case should also be a doubt, and the contrast with שמואל's case falls apart again.

keyTerms.meaning: It turned to vinegar (Aramaic form)

phrases.english: Here too:
phrases.notes: Now "here" means the barrel of wine.

phrases.english: it is now that it has turned to vinegar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 26 to undo the answer of step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between the wine and the woman
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'only now' argument applies equally to the vinegar, so the wine's חזקה is not really broken either.

steps.title: Two weaknesses against one
steps.stepSummary: The barrel case has two strikes against the separation working; the woman's case has only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, there are two weaknesses. Here, there is only one weakness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final distinction. In the barrel there are two reasons to say the separation failed, and with the woman there is only one reason to say she was a בוגרת back then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the barrel, the wine is vinegar now, and the טבל also has a חזקה of never having been fixed. With the woman, the only point against her old status is that she is a בוגרת now. Two weaknesses together give a definite ruling, but one alone leaves שמואל's case a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Two points of weakness
Only one point of weakness
There (the other case)

steps.whatToRemember: The barrel case is definite because two factors work together: it is vinegar now, and the טבל has its original חזקה. The woman's case has only her present state as a בוגרת, so it stays a doubt, as שמואל rules.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general idea: what we see now, standing alone, may not decide the past. When it is joined by a חזקה pointing the same way, it can give a definite ruling.

phrases.english: There, there are two points of weakness,
phrases.notes: The two points: the wine is vinegar now, and the טבל's original status from step 22.

phrases.english: here, it is only one point of weakness
that there is.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם תַּרְתֵּי לְרֵיעוּתָא, הָכָא חֲדָא לְרֵיעוּתָא הוּא דְּאִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 27 and closes the comparison
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counting the weakening factors (two against one)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each case has one weakening factor, so they should be treated alike
steps.terutzMaskana: The barrel has two weakening factors, so it is definite; the woman has one, so it is a doubt

steps.title: Maybe this is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new try: perhaps שמואל's ruling matches one side of a מחלוקת of תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say it is like a dispute between תנאים:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to bring a ברייתא to see if our question is really a מחלוקת of תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled here yet. The גמרא suggests that the question of how much 'what we see now' decides the past may already be argued over by תנאים, and the source comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say; introduces a suggestion
Like a dispute between תנאים

phrases.english: Let us say it is parallel to a dispute between tanna'im:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the comparison, opens a new attempt to link the issue to a תנאים dispute
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether שמואל's view depends on a known disagreement among תנאים
